extracted.intended_audience: apprenticeship program sponsors, State Apprenticeship Agencies (SAAs), Registration Agencies, employers, Office of Apprenticeship staff, and public commenters
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts proposed regulatory standards and evaluative metrics for registered apprenticeship programs under the Department's NPRM, including data collection, program quality metrics, equity and accountability requirements, definitions, and a new CTE apprenticeship model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform national data collection / disaggregation
rubrics_metrics.description: Developing a data collection framework that collects uniform data elements on a nationwide basis in order to disaggregate such data (such as by race and ethnicity, industry, occupation, from a State or national perspective) and assess information that accurately compares program outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposal seeks more uniform and consistent approach to data collection and analysis to derive accurate, timely, and consequential insights about registered apprenticeship on a nationwide basis and to enable data-driven decisions and improvements throughout the National Apprenticeship System.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collection of interim credentials / industry-recognized certifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Require program sponsors to provide data on the interim credentials or other industry-recognized certifications offered through their programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to understand prevalence and usefulness of interim credentials, incentivize leveraging recognized postsecondary credentials into program design, and enhance portability and national recognition for credentials obtained in programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of career wage profile in occupational suitability determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Require that applications for a determination on an occupation's suitability for registered apprenticeship training include information relating to the career wage profile of the subject occupation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assists in ensuring that determinations on occupations' suitability consider wage-related career outcomes; referenced as proposed inclusion at 29 CFR 29.7(b)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Collection of pre-apprenticeship engagement and placement data
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect information from sponsors on pre-apprenticeship program engagement and placement as part of the proposed rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aims to provide clarity about pre-apprenticeship programs, enable data collection from sponsors, and promote alignment with other Federal workforce investments that may support pre-apprenticeship models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collection of postsecondary academic credit and industry-recognized credentials acquired by apprentices
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritize collecting information on both postsecondary academic credit and industry-recognized credentials that apprentices acquire as part of their participation in registered apprenticeship programs, in addition to their acquisition of Certificates of Completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows students, job seekers, and workers to make better informed choices regarding career needs and contributes to measures like credential rate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program standards must convey competencies and lead to occupational proficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that all registered apprenticeship programs convey competencies and lead to occupational proficiency for apprentices who complete programs (proposed consolidation of apprenticeship training models at proposed 29 CFR 29.8(a)(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part 29 standards of apprenticeship are used to apply quality standards consistently; proposed updates would strengthen program-level requirements to ensure occupational proficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections against unreasonable training costs and restrictions on labor market mobility
rubrics_metrics.description: Enhanced protections for apprentices against unreasonable training costs and restrictions on their labor market mobility (proposed at 29 CFR 29.9).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed as part of program quality enhancements to protect apprentices' welfare and well-being.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embedding equity: sponsor strategies for recruitment, hiring, and retention
rubrics_metrics.description: Require all sponsors seeking registration of an apprenticeship program to articulate an equitable, intentional, and achievable strategy for advancing the program's recruitment, hiring, and retention of individuals from underserved communities, including through documented partnerships with pre-apprenticeship or registered CTE apprenticeship programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aligns part 29 with part 30 EEO elements; sponsors must identify and reduce barriers to enrollment and completion for individuals from all underserved communities; registered programs must adhere to non-discrimination and EEO requirements in part 30.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment and centralization of definitions at 29.2
rubrics_metrics.description: Set forth all applicable definitions governing 29 CFR parts 29 and 30 at 29 CFR 29.2 to centralize definitions and eliminate duplication/inconsistency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizational change to reduce confusion and regulatory burden; comments on substance should reference 29 CFR 29.2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability: sponsor and participating employer responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that both registered apprenticeship program sponsors and any employers that have adopted the sponsor's standards of apprenticeship ('participating employers') are responsible for adhering to the minimum labor standards in 29 CFR part 29 and the EEO requirements in 29 CFR part 30.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed rule would also require sponsors of group programs to screen and actively monitor participating employers to ensure compliance; strengthens accountability so apprentices are afforded required rights and protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: SAA recognition, State planning, and minimum standards for SAAs
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish a State planning framework for recognition of SAAs that delineates roles and responsibilities, criteria around SAAs' approval of apprenticeship programs for Federal purposes, and ensures coordination and minimum standards to safeguard apprentice safety and welfare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission of State Apprenticeship Plans would occur on a cyclical basis to allow OA to review plans and provide technical assistance; includes corrective action planning if full approval not granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-part regulatory structure (Subparts A, B, C)
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose §§29.1–29.6 applicable to entire part and three subparts: Subpart A (standards for registered apprenticeship programs), Subpart B (registered CTE apprenticeship model), Subpart C (Administration and Coordination of the National Apprenticeship System).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subpart A updates approval of occupations suitable for apprenticeship, registration standards, apprenticeship agreements, and development of quality labor standards; Subpart B addresses registering under the CTE model; Subpart C addresses reporting, SAA recognition/planning, and information sharing to integrate apprenticeship into other laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'apprentice' (scope and minimum age)
rubrics_metrics.description: Modify 'apprentice' to mean an individual participating in a program subject to the requirements of 29 CFR parts 29 and 30, rather than any apprenticeship program; an apprentice must be a worker at least 16 years of age (except where higher minimum age fixed by law).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aligns with the Fair Labor Standards Act and its implementing regulations; clarification confines regulatory coverage to programs governed by parts 29 and 30.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for 'apprenticeship agreement'
rubrics_metrics.description: An apprenticeship agreement must satisfy each applicable regulatory requirement in proposed §29.9, describe terms and conditions of employment and training of the apprentice, and may include subsequent contractual provisions or agreements between the apprentice and sponsor (or participating employer) during the apprenticeship term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed definition ties the agreement to the operative requirements in §29.9 and clarifies scope of contractual documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'cancellation' limited to apprenticeship agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Modify 'cancellation' to reflect that an apprenticeship agreement may be canceled by either the apprentice or the sponsor and remove concept of cancellation of a program (voluntary deregistration covers program end).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposes voluntary deregistration as the process for programs seeking to end registration status; cancels only apply to agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinct certificate definitions and purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish standalone definitions for documentary evidence: 'Certificate of Completion', 'certificate of completion of registered CTE apprenticeship', 'Certificate of Participation', 'Certificate of Recognition', and 'Certificate of Registration'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies different functional types of documentary evidence for purposes like proposed §29.18, §29.30, or other purposes (e.g., Certificate of Completion = Registration Agency determination apprentice completed a registered program; Certificate of Participation = documents participation; Certificate of Recognition = OA approval of National Guidelines; Certificate of Registration = Registration Agency registered a program).

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual completion rate (new program quality measure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Add 'annual completion rate' calculated by identifying all the apprentices who leave a program during a fiscal year as the denominator and the number of those who complete the program as the numerator; unlike the proposed cohort completion rate, this measure would not exclude exiters during the probationary period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Would be part of data requirements at proposed §29.25 and subject to program reviews under proposed §29.19; useful for identifying programs exiting significant numbers of apprentices without graduating them and aligning with ETP reporting under WIOA; Department solicits comments on probationary period treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohort completion rate (revised definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define 'cohort completion rate' as the percentage of an apprenticeship cohort (group of individual apprentices registered to a specific program during a given fiscal year) that receives a Certificate of Completion within 1 year of the projected completion date; continues to explain when an apprentice will not be included in the calculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This distinguishes cohort completion from annual completion rate and retains exclusion of exiters during the probationary period for cohort measures to avoid disincentivizing programs from recruiting participants who leave early.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credential rate (new metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Add 'credential rate' to calculate the percentage of registered apprenticeship program completers in a cohort that receive an interim credential (not including Certificates of Completion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to incentivize leveraging recognized postsecondary credentials and industry-recognized credentials into program design; programs are not required to offer interim credentials; metric excludes apprentices whose participation ends during probationary period; not intended as sole indicator of program quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competency definition aligned to competency frameworks
rubrics_metrics.description: Modify 'competency' to describe the attainment of knowledge, skills, and abilities specified in a work process schedule and include measurable attainment of techniques (hands-on practices such as physical use of equipment and tools).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removes phrasing limited to 'manual, mechanical or technical skills' to align with frameworks like O*NET, DOL competency models, and competency-based occupational frameworks used to develop work process schedules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collective bargaining agreement definition and role
rubrics_metrics.description: Define 'collective bargaining agreement' as written agreement between an employer (or group of employers) and bargaining representative(s) of a labor union covering wages, hours, safety, benefits, and other terms; when applicable, CBAs inform development of program standards and typically govern employer participation in group programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides clarity about the meaning and use of CBAs in the proposed rule; Department seeks comments to increase clarification on this term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrective action plan for State Apprenticeship Plan deficiencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Define 'corrective action plan' as the product required when a State Apprenticeship Plan is not granted full approval by the Department (described in proposed §29.27).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designed to provide SAAs with clear actions to take to become eligible for full approval of the State Apprenticeship Plan.
